news.title: NZ squad named for FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup
news.lede: Head coach Callum Holmes has named his 21-player squad for the FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup in Poland set for September 5 – 27. There is still some concern for the tournament over possible boycotts by different nations regarding FIFA leadership. NZ Tall Ferns just beaten by Brazil. However he French Football Federation was first to clarify that it would participate in the upcoming U=20 World Cup, followed by support from New Zealand, and later Canada and Brazil.

news.title: World Cup red card 'troubled' Howard Webb as conspiracy theorists slammed
news.lede: Pro Ref (formerly PGMOL) chief Howard Webb insists he was left "really troubled" by the decision to overturn Folarin Balogun's World Cup red card following political interference. Webb, who is about to embark on his fifth season as Chief Refereeing Officer, notes the call has sparked unfair claims of widespread "corruption" - which he feels is incredibly dangerous for the game's image. The 55-year-old said: "I was really troubled by it, really. I don't know the ins and outs of the process, obviously, what happened in the end, but the fact that we know... well, what do we know?

news.title: Azcárraga: ‘I don’t see a World Cup in Mexico in 2038 as a far-fetched idea’
news.lede: The 2026 World Cup, co-hosted by Mexico, Canada and the USA left a hugely positive lasting impression on everyone who attended matches in Mexico City, Guadalajara and Monterrey; indeed, many wondered why there were only a handful of matches played on Mexican soil. Amid such euphoria, fans wondered whether Mexico would ever host another football festival, and to everyone’s surprise, the prospect of another men’s tournament is not so far off. At an interview with TUDN, Emilio Azcárraga Jean, president of Club América and an influential figure in Mexican football with contacts within the FMF (Mexican FA), said that hosting another men’s World Cup on Mexican soil in 2038 is not far-fetched. With confederation rotation, the conditions could align within three cycles.

news.title: Fears World Cup row over Folarin Balogun could fuel Prem conspiracy theories
news.lede: REF chief Howard Webb fears the World Cup row over USA striker Folarin Balogun could fuel false PREM conspiracy theories. Pro Ref boss Webb admitted he was “troubled” after the intervention by US President Donald Trump saw Balogun cleared to play against Belgium despite his red card for serious foul play being confirmed. And the former whistler conceded his concerns that intervention in football governance by outside figures could convince some fans that the entire game is suspect. Webb said: “I was really troubled by it.

news.title: AFA president Claudio Tapia lashes out at Argentina’s World Cup final conspiracy theories
news.lede: A month after Argentina fell 1-0 to Spain in overtime at the 2026 World Cup final, Argentine Football Association (AFA) president Claudio Tapia broke his silence with a lengthy, pointed statement on social media, taking direct aim at what he called a “miserable campaign” to paint the national team as having thrown the match. The backlash stems from a wave of conspiracy theories that spread in Argentina in the weeks following the loss, some of them tied to a leaked video showing Lionel Messi delivering an unusually calm pre-match speech in the locker room, in which he told his teammates to “forget about everything”. That clip was seized on by some to suggest the players had mentally checked out before kickoff, and it wasn’t long before speculation grew into open accusations, with some in Argentina even floating the idea that the squad had deliberately “given away” the final.

news.title: One month after World Cup final, Argentine Football Association president explodes against conspiracists
news.lede: One month ago, Spain won the World Cup final against Argentina, and a series of conspiracy theories, some implying that they had lost on purpose for a variety or reasons, like threats by FIFA, secret deals, or anything but to accept that they had not been better than their rivals. Today, Claudio "Chiqui" Tapia, President of the Argentine Football Association, has written a strongly worded statement slamming all of those who started those conspiracy theories and of course were never proved." A month since that final. A month since the lies, the manipulation, and a despicable campaign to portray this team as having thrown the game.

news.title: Richard Masters and Howard Webb criticise FIFA over Folarin Balogun's red card controversy at 2026 World Cup
news.lede: Two of the most powerful men in English football have joined forces to hit out at FIFA and the U-turn which allowed USA striker Folarin Balogun to play on at the World Cup last month, despite the red card which should have led to an automatic ban. Richard Masters , the chief executive of the Premier League and Howard Webb , the chief refereeing officer in England, say the decision undermines faith in football at all levels of the game. Balogun was sent off in the last 32 match against Bosnia & Herzegovina which led to an automatic ban under World Cup rules, without the opportunity for appeal, or for the ban to be reduced.
